NYISO.note: FRONTIER WITHDRAWN — NYISO reverts to NOT-YET (2026-07-19 phantom-outage re-audit, the ERCOT-79 cross-ISO lane). The 2026-07-11 frontier and the 2026-07-13 calibration-complete marker rested on keeper nyiso-62, solved against a STALE-detector unit-outage extract (campd-unit-outages-NYISO.csv, 1,598 rows, mtime 2026-07-16) that predated the 2026-07-17 detector consolidation. Regenerating on the consolidated detector yields 2,641 rows (+1,056 real outage windows the stale detector under-counted — exactly the 1,598-vs-2,641 gap the 2026-07-12 intake_log flagged as owed adjudication). Re-solving the nyiso-62 recipe VERBATIM on the corrected extract (2026-07-13-nyiso-63-phantom-outage) flips the determination CALIBRATED-WITH-CAVEATS -> NOT-YET: C1 fuel-mix FAIL (2024 ST_GAS -3.36 TWh), C3a mean LMP FAIL (2023 +25.0%, model $30.6->$47.2 vs actual $31 — a +51% overshoot), C3b shape FAIL (2023 NRMSE 0.385); ST_GAS sheds ~1.1-1.5 TWh/yr into peakers every year. The keeper's offer curves were silently compensating for the under-counted outages (rule 11) — its calibration is co-dependent on the inaccurate availability envelope, the ERCOT-79 condition exactly. DETERMINATION: NOT-YET on accurate data. HOLDOUT BLOCKED: the calibration-complete marker is suspended (see calibration-complete.json withdrawn block) so the touch-once one-shot (2019, H1-2026) is NOT spent on a keeper that fails on accurate data (rule 22). OPEN LANE (successor): re-calibrate NYISO offer curves against the corrected outages across the full 2023-2025 span (keep the accurate input, fix the root cause — rule 11; rule 16). Contrast NEISO, which HOLDS calibrated on its corrected extract (neiso-60, PJM-115 fix-in-place pattern). See results/calibration/FINDING-neiso-nyiso-phantom-outage-reaudit-2026-07-19.md.

ERCOT.note: FRONTIER WITHDRAWN — ERCOT reverts to NOT-YET (owner directive 2026-07-17, the ERCOT-79 availability-envelope audit: 'we can't have a keeper on inaccurate data'). The 2026-07-17 frontier declaration rested on a keeper (ercot76) whose scarcity tail was formed on a PHANTOM CAMPD facility-outage bug: the run-based detector hard-zeroed ~1.9-5.7 GW of daily-cycling combined-cycle capability its own CEMS shows generating (T H Wharton et al.), artificially exhausting the event-time fleet so the co-opt priced into its ORDC steps. ERCOT-79 found and fixed the detector (event-based detection for cycling classes; source-faithful, measured CEMS + EIA-930, validated 58h false-outage 1,904->0 MW/h, 0% genuine-outage over-correction) and the fix was ADOPTED (corrected campd-outages.csv installed). On the corrected fleet the keeper recipe (re-solved as keeper 2026-07-17-ercot79-corrected-outages) resolves the 2023 summer over-shoot ($1,068->$242, confirming ERCOT-78) but UN-CATCHES the real scarcity tail (2023 C3c 179->53 vs RT 181, Aug caught 71->25, 2025 tail 19->0) — the offer/scarcity calibration was tuned against the phantom-tightened fleet. DETERMINATION: NOT-YET (C3a/C3b/C3c fail on accurate data). OPEN LANE (successor): a full ERCOT offer-curve + ORDC/co-opt re-calibration against the corrected availability envelope, so the real scarcity re-forms on real fleet tightness. CROSS-ISO: the detector is shared — PJM's committed facility csv shows a stronger phantom signature and all six ISOs' unit-level extracts use it; each ISO is its own regenerate-and-re-audit lane. See results/calibration/FINDING-ercot79-phantom-outage-2026-07.md.
